review.reviewer: independent PH-228 implementation reviewer (fresh context, read-only; multi-round)
findings: Round 1 blockers fixed: inactive counterparty payees and inactive employees are rejected at new writes/identifications with status and active/inactive business-date windows; draft own-account payees rejected; opening_cents/opening_on frozen by model, service, CheckConstraint and SQLite/PostgreSQL UPDATE triggers; PostgreSQL match/receipt guards now raise SQLSTATE 23514; identify/reverse semantics frozen (single unreversed identification, reverse only current effective match, re-identify after reverse allowed).

Round 1 replay blocker fixed: structural payee normalization and digest first, then receipt replay, then external-key same-input replay, and only then live party/account state validation. Regression test proves deactivated counterparty/employee still replay the original transaction/match with no new facts, while new writes and changed inputs still reject.

Reviewer accepted the disclosed counterparty_id UUID deviation (no cross-owner FK) because a real FK would force the cash plugin to require contracts and re-break four existing test disable-order sites outside PH-228 whitelist; writes validate the counterparty through the named contracts service and verify_integrity checks same-organization existence. Residual risk: direct SQL could create orphans; DB-level FK would need separate planning.

Retained minors recorded in unverified: verify_integrity does not validate evidence/external-key format, payee JSON shape, current active state of historical identified payees, receipt refs or direct-SQL orphans; UI counterparty dropdown may show inactive parties (server rejects); browser Chromium-only; PostgreSQL races and production/UAT unverified.
review.evidence: Reviewer reran the full suite (711 OK, 43 skip), the 31 cash tests (22 backend + 6 HTTP + 3 PG-only skip), probes for deactivation replay and opening-freeze IntegrityError, check/makemigrations, verify_integrity on the real cash browser database and upgraded legacy/populated copies (all ok:true), and parsed browser evidence on final HEAD c2f2f71 (36/36, dirty=false, 0 server 500s). Formal PASS is conditional on the PR PostgreSQL CI executing the 3 cash concurrency tests successfully.

deviations: cash plugin manifest keeps requires={} and default_enabled=True; counterparty/employee reads use named contracts/core interfaces at service entry with module-enabled checks, so no new plugin dependency edge or test disable-order changes are introduced.
Counterparty is stored as a validated UUID field rather than a cross-owner database FK, preserving the owner boundary; cash writes never read contracts tables directly.

Drafts are not projected as canonical FundingAccount/CashTransaction entities and no canonical cash event is written; generic cash.* audits still create non-canonical DomainEvents through the existing audit helper.
No ledger/Balance integration exists yet: cash facts are recorded but not posted; posting/classification is the next planning slot's priority and PH-169 is not complete.

Browser evidence on HEAD 2c71e9c: 32/32 checks pass, 0 failures; owner/finance write, auditor read-only, pm/member 403; payee never rendered as raw JSON; identify/reverse history visible; CSRF 403; 320-1440 no overflow; cash-disabled routes 403 while service history stays readable; 0 server 500s.

Accepted deviation: CashTransaction.counterparty_id remains a validated UUIDField instead of a cross-owner database FK. A real FK would force the cash plugin manifest to require contracts, which in turn re-breaks four existing test disable-order sites that PH-228 has no whitelist to change; writes still validate the counterparty through the named contracts service including status and active/inactive business-date windows, and this deviation is disclosed here.

Replay ordering is frozen: structural payee normalization and input digest first, then receipt replay, then external-key same-input replay, and only then live party/account state validation. Later counterparty/employee/account deactivation therefore cannot invalidate an existing fact replay.

PostgreSQL guards for CashPartyMatch/CashReceipt use dedicated guard functions raising SQLSTATE 23514 (not the generic P0001 helper), and FundingAccount opening_cents/opening_on are frozen by a database UPDATE trigger on both SQLite and PostgreSQL.

verify_integrity was extended: all funding accounts must have opening_cents=0 and opening_on, cash payee/identified counterparty/employee/own_account refs must exist in the same organization, reverse matches are unique, and no AccountingEvent may use the cash namespace.

Activation and draft-edit races are resolved with conditional version+status UPDATE statements so exactly one worker writes the state change and its receipt; concurrency tests assert baseline+1 receipts and one-winner semantics.
unverified: PostgreSQL concurrency (3 tests) is executed by the PR CI job; local SQLite skips are not evidence.
Cash posting, classification, allocation, clearing (PH-170), refunds (PH-171), bank-file import, opening balances, production/customer UAT remain unverified/not implemented; PH-169 is not complete.

Browser evidence covers Chromium 320/390/768/1024/1440 only, and the browser run did not click the account-activation button itself (activation was seeded through the real service; HTTP tests cover the UI activation path).

verify_integrity does not validate evidence/external-key formats, payee JSON shape, receipt references, or the current active state of historical identified payees (historical facts may reference later-deactivated parties by design).
counterparty_id has no database FK (accepted deviation); direct SQL could create an orphan counterparty id, mitigated only by service checks and verify_integrity same-org existence checks.
UI counterparty dropdown may still list inactive parties; the server rejects such writes with a business error, but filtering the list is a future UX improvement.
